overview: The Medford Public Schools School Committee serves as the governing body for the city's public school district, responsible for approving annual operating budgets, establishing district policies, appointing and evaluating the superintendent, and overseeing school facilities and capital improvement projects. Across the span from May 2021 through October 2026, the committee conducted its business through regular and special sessions alongside targeted subcommittees covering areas such as rules and policy, strategic planning, and building projects. Its work has included managing pandemic recovery protocols, navigating complex collective bargaining with multiple union units, addressing district-wide space constraints, and advancing long-term facilities improvements in partnership with the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA). The body also managed executive leadership turnover, transitioning from Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent to Interim and then permanent Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi. As of the most recent meetings in autumn 2026, the committee is engaged in advancing schematic designs and feasibility selections for MSBA capital projects across the high school and elementary schools, refining district elementary reassignment policies, and formulating a new multi-year strategic plan.

threads.name: Medford High School building project
threads.summary: The committee initiated efforts to address aging infrastructure at Medford High School by authorizing an initial Statement of Interest to the MSBA Core Program in 2022 (M24#3, M26#1). Following invitation into the MSBA Core Program eligibility phase in late 2023, the committee established the Medford Comprehensive High School Building Committee and approved its membership structure and project goals (M70#5, M74#5, M75#5, M80#8). In 2025, the committee completed the eligibility phase with a certified enrollment target of 1,395 students, authorized a feasibility study agreement, and selected Left Field as the Owner's Project Manager (M111#7, M112#4, M119#5). During 2026, the building committee and School Committee narrowed design options, eliminated configurations conflicting with a 1967 DCR deed restriction on Edgerly Field, adopted an educational plan, and established LEED v4 Silver, net-zero, and Teen Health Center project priorities (M136#3, M148#2, M151#3, M155#6, M155#7). Membership updates were approved in August 2026 as the project entered its schematic design phase (M156#9).

threads.name: Superintendent leadership and evaluation
threads.summary: Throughout 2021 and 2023, the committee conducted annual goal-setting and performance evaluations for Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent using standardized state frameworks (M05#1, M12#7, M34#5, M56#2, M59#2). In mid-2024, the committee entered extended executive sessions concerning superintendent contract negotiations (M90#2, M92#2, M96#1, M97#1). In December 2024, the committee appointed Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as Interim Superintendent effective January 2025, honoring Dr. Edouard-Vincent upon her departure after seven years of service (M106#2, M108#5, M108#9). In February 2026, following annual evaluation feedback, the committee voted to appoint Dr. Galusi as permanent superintendent, subsequently approving a three-year contract and realigning the annual evaluation schedule to the academic school year (M135#6, M136#4, M146#6, M153#11).

threads.name: District facilities and HVAC capital upgrades
threads.summary: Facing recurring cooling system failures and water leaks across aging infrastructure, the committee authorized major building assessments and repairs across multiple schools (M10#6, M62#6, M82#6). In April 2024, the committee approved a $15 to $20 million decarbonization scope for Andrews and McGlynn middle schools, while adopting a policy prohibiting new fossil-fuel equipment purchases without committee authorization (M82#6, M82#13). The committee subsequently approved bond requests totaling over $25 million and authorized Construction Management at Risk for the McGlynn and Andrews HVAC projects (M103#6, M107#6, M116#7). In 2025 and 2026, work expanded to elementary schools through MSBA Accelerated Repair applications, resulting in the approval of a $22.7 million schematic design and CMR delivery for Roberts Elementary and the selection of a ground-source geothermal HVAC system for Missituk Elementary (M114#1, M153#5, M156#4, M160#4, M160#5).

threads.name: Elementary capacity and school space utilization
threads.summary: District capacity pressures escalated in 2024, when severe overcrowding at Roberts Elementary prompted calls for formal redistricting and long-term space planning (M93#8, M94#6). The committee initiated formal reviews of enrollment disparities in spring 2025, directing the administration to evaluate space data (M117#4). In June 2025, the committee voted to relocate early childhood MEEP classrooms from Roberts to Missituk to relieve space deficits and established a strategic space planning task force (M122#6, M122#7). An architectural space utilization study proposed reconfiguring grades to K-4, 5-6, and 7-8 spans, but the committee voted in July 2026 to delay any middle school grade configuration changes to the 2028-2029 school year (M131#5, M132#5, M155#4). In October 2026, the committee took up a draft policy to regulate elementary reassignment requests and manage school capacity buffers (M159#5).

threads.name: Labor relations and collective bargaining
threads.summary: Collective bargaining negotiations formed a continuous item across executive sessions, marked by prolonged discussions with the Medford Teachers Association (MTA) starting in 2022 when talks reached a formal impasse and state mediation before a four-year contract was ratified (M28#8, M33#5, M37#4, M38#3, M43#5). In parallel, the committee settled multiple agreements for nurses, paraprofessionals, secretaries, custodians, and administrators across successive rounds (M34#1, M36#2, M64#1, M88#2, M91#2, M91#3, M121#6, M125#2, M127#1). A successor three-year agreement with the MTA was ratified in April 2025, extending the school day by 15 minutes (M118#3). During 2026, the committee continued regular bargaining sessions, ratifying a contract with cafeteria workers while handling ongoing grievance hearings and contract strategy with administrative and instructional units (M139#1, M149#2, M150#1, M153#1, M157#1).

threads.name: Student safety, climate, and discipline policy
threads.summary: Following high school disciplinary incidents and a bathroom stabbing in late 2022, the committee engaged consultant Michael Welch to review school culture, climate, and security procedures (M12#4, M12#12, M43#4, M44#5, M44#6). The administration instituted a 10-point safety plan, student tracking mechanisms, and adopted the Panorama survey tool to measure school climate (M44#5, M45#4, M49#6, M66#5). The committee conducted extensive reviews of out-of-school suspensions, updated the district Bullying Prevention and Intervention Plan (Policy JICFB) to include parental notice and language translation, and adopted a non-discrimination policy protecting gender identity (M12#10, M14#8, M41#11, M60#4, M60#6, M68#6, M73#7). In 2024 and 2025, the committee allocated capital funding for high school bathroom safety and vape detection, received comprehensive discipline reports, and updated restraint and bullying policies to ensure DESE compliance (M82#7, M105#9, M123#13, M147#6).

threads.name: Student transportation operations and safety
threads.summary: Student transportation faced persistent disruptions due to regional school bus driver shortages, resulting in canceled routes, boarding delays, and distance eligibility adjustments (M06#6, M09#2, M33#3, M93#12, M94#8). The committee developed a community transportation survey in 2024 to assess needs prior to reprocuring transportation contracts (M66#8, M79#1). In June 2025, the committee approved a new five-year yellow bus contract with Eastern Bus while referring bus electrification feasibility to subcommittee (M123#4). To address route safety and student conduct, the committee approved requesting city adoption of automated bus stop-arm cameras, introduced rotating paraprofessionals as afternoon bus monitors, and hired a dedicated transportation manager (M126#8, M128#5, M129#6, M140#4). In autumn 2026, the Student Advisory Council reported on a newly added high school late bus service expanding access to extracurriculars (M159#4).

threads.name: Curriculum, assessments, and graduation standards
threads.summary: The committee routinely reviewed district assessment benchmarks, integrating NWEA MAP diagnostic testing across grades K-12 alongside state MCAS results (M09#4, M31#8, M37#5, M39#6, M69#4, M102#5). Following multi-year curriculum reviews, the district adopted Investigations 3 for elementary math and HMH 'Into Reading' for core elementary literacy (M23#5, M45#6, M58#5). Following the passage of statewide ballot Question 2 in November 2024, the committee approved revisions to Policy IKF, replacing MCAS competency determinations for high school graduation with successful completion of aligned coursework in English, math, and science (M95#8, M111#3, M113#7, M117#3). The committee also rescinded its obsolete MCAS policy, updated CTE admissions to a non-weighted lottery, and adopted policies governing the use of generative AI in schools (M123#9, M128#3, M132#7, M153#10).
